title: Affine-local constructibility of pro-etale modules over discrete Noetherian rings
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $R$ a discrete commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. On the small pro-etale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], use the constant ring sheaf $\underline R_X$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and its module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. A module sheaf $F$ is affine-locally constructible if for every affine open $U\subseteq X$ there is a finite locally closed scheme stratification $S$ of $U$ [def-constructible-stratification], with each part constructible in $U$ [def-weil-constructible-subset], such that for each stratum immersion $i_a:Z_a\to U\to X$ its module inverse image $i_a^*F$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] is locally isomorphic, on the localized ringed sites, to constant sheaves of finitely presented $R$-modules [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Explicitly, for every object $V$ of $(Z_a)_{\mathrm{proet}}$ there is a covering sieve $T$ on $V$ such that for every $W\to V$ in $T$ there is a finitely presented $R$-module $M$ and a module-sheaf isomorphism $(i_a^*F)|_W\simeq\underline M|_W$. The constant module on the localized ringed site is the existing simultaneous constant-ring/module sheafification construction [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. No finiteness of the underlying sets and no invertibility assumption is imposed.
